sources.title: Rust csv 1.4.0 Reader implementation
sources.version_commit: csv crate 1.4.0; docs.rs release build; commit not identified on this page
sources.locator: reader.rs: default ReaderBuilder fields (around lines 47-55); delimiter/header/flexible methods (150-192, 316-319); record iterator (2079-2092); error policy docs (691-700)
sources.observed_operation: Opened versioned docs.rs source for ReaderBuilder defaults and record iteration; inspected source lines via the source view.
sources.governing_conditions: Default delimiter is comma, first record is a header, flexible record lengths are disabled, and iterator reads records incrementally. A custom delimiter is configured on the builder. Parser's general salvage-oriented parsing policy still requires application-level shape and type validation.
sources.applicability: Candidate low-memory parser for delimited text. Treat every field as raw text first; enable variable widths only to capture/report row-level shape errors, then compare width to the selected header.

critic_review.observed_operation: Directly opened csv 1.4.0 source; confirmed comma/header/fixed-width defaults, configurable dialect, and record iteration. Application still owns row and field validation.

sources.title: Rust csv 1.4.0 Position API
sources.locator: Position description and byte(), line(), record() methods, lines 59-93
sources.observed_operation: Opened exact versioned Position API documentation.
sources.governing_conditions: Byte offsets and record indices start at zero; line numbers start at one; the reader associates a position with each record.
sources.applicability: Keep byte offset and logical record index as stable invalid-row references. Use displayed physical line as supplementary only because an upstream CRLF line-accounting report remains open (SRC04).

critic_review.observed_operation: Opened exact-version Position API; byte offset and record index start at zero, line number at one.

sources.title: Rust csv 1.4.0 Reader and encoding/error behavior
sources.locator: Reader record API, builder configuration, and error/UTF-8 discussion, lines 73-103 of the versioned page
sources.observed_operation: Opened versioned Reader documentation and checked the record-oriented API and errors.
sources.governing_conditions: Reader supports record-by-record raw fields. StringRecord parsing requires UTF-8; invalid UTF-8 errors. ByteRecord accepts raw bytes, while non-UTF-8 text requires explicit transcoding.
sources.applicability: Preserve source strings, avoid direct Serde coercion to quantity/code types, and make any alternate encoding an explicit supplier-profile or staff choice.

critic_review.observed_operation: Checked csv 1.4.0 StringRecord/Reader docs: StringRecord enforces UTF-8; ByteRecord preserves arbitrary bytes; another encoding requires transcoding.

sources.title: rust-csv issue #395: CRLF line position accounting
sources.version_commit: Upstream issue #395 opened 2025-04-02; Open at access; linked PR #433 is also Open and unmerged at 2026-10-12T00:44:31Z; no released fix was observed
sources.locator: Problem statement and minimal reproducer, lines 160-186; status Open at access
sources.observed_operation: Opened upstream issue and reviewed the reported reproduction and status.
sources.governing_conditions: The issue describes stale line positions for CRLF after record reads. A linked open PR proposes consuming complete CRLF terminators; it is not part of released csv 1.4.0 on evidence reviewed.
sources.applicability: Do not promise physical line numbers as the sole audit location. Store raw byte offset and logical record index and verify CRLF in proposed tests.

critic_review.observed_operation: Opened issue #395: post-read CRLF line position can remain on the prior line; issue and linked PR #433 were Open.

sources.title: rust-csv issue #377: duplicate header deserialization
sources.version_commit: Issue report against rust-csv repository; opened 2024-12-21; Open at access
sources.locator: Duplicate-field example and maintainer response, lines 156-184
sources.observed_operation: Opened upstream feature discussion about duplicate column headers.
sources.governing_conditions: Serde mapping of duplicate field names is ambiguous and no general vector-based deserializer solution was accepted in the response.
sources.applicability: Read supplier headers as a positional record, reject or require manual resolution for duplicate headers after the chosen normalization, and do not auto-map duplicate labels.

critic_review.observed_operation: Opened issue #377: duplicate-header Serde discussion remains Open; maintainer says vector deserialization is uncertain and notes tail ambiguity.

sources.title: rust_decimal 1.43.0 Decimal::from_str_exact
sources.locator: from_str_exact signature and underflow condition, lines 616-625
sources.observed_operation: Opened the current versioned Decimal API and its exact parsing method.
sources.governing_conditions: Exact parser converts a decimal string and returns an error when value cannot be represented at the given scale; it is not a locale detector.
sources.applicability: Candidate after an explicit supplier decimal/grouping convention is confirmed and validated. Keep original text; reject ambiguous forms before canonicalization.

critic_review.observed_operation: Opened Decimal::from_str_exact docs at 1.43.0; it errors on underflow/unrepresentable scale and does not select locale separators.

sources.title: encoding_rs 0.8.42 Encoding and strict decoding
sources.observed_operation: Reviewed crate documentation on explicit encoding labels, streaming decoders, and no-replacement decoding.
sources.governing_conditions: The crate exposes explicit encodings and strict variants that signal malformed input instead of substituting replacement characters. Streaming inputs use decoder objects rather than whole-buffer helpers.
sources.applicability: Optional route for supplier encodings beyond UTF-8. Select a label explicitly and fail malformed sequences; do not silently replace bytes.

critic_review.observed_operation: Checked encoding_rs 0.8.42 docs/search excerpts: no-replacement paths report malformed sequences; replacement paths substitute U+FFFD; Decoder supports streaming. Exact Encoding page did not render.

sources.title: Polars 0.55.2 CSV read options
sources.locator: with_schema, with_infer_schema_length, with_ignore_errors method docs, especially lines 254-271
sources.observed_operation: Opened versioned Polars CSV read configuration and checked schema inference and parser-error controls.
sources.governing_conditions: Schema inference defaults to 100 rows; a full scan is available but documented as slow; ignore_errors continues to the next batch after a ParserError.
sources.applicability: Viable dataframe alternative for bulk analytics, but type inference and error skipping can hide later-row code/quantity differences unless schema is forced to text and every skipped/error row is explicitly surfaced.

critic_review.observed_operation: Opened polars-io 0.55.2 docs: inference defaults to 100 rows; with_ignore_errors continues after ParserError.

sources.title: SQLite transaction semantics
sources.version_commit: Current SQLite online documentation; unversioned page, accessed 2026-10-12
sources.observed_operation: Opened SQLite's transaction, lock, busy, and transaction-error documentation.
sources.governing_conditions: Transactions are DEFERRED by default; IMMEDIATE reserves write intent earlier; SQLite supports only one simultaneous writer; some errors may roll back one statement or the whole transaction, so callers should explicitly restore/verify state.
sources.applicability: Conditional example only if the product database is SQLite. The proposal requires the actual database adapter's transaction, concurrency and rollback behavior to be verified before writes.

critic_review.observed_operation: Opened SQLite transaction docs: default DEFERRED; read-to-write upgrade may return SQLITE_BUSY; some errors require explicit rollback/state verification.

sources.title: SQLite atomic commit
sources.version_commit: Current SQLite online documentation; unversioned page, accessed 2026-10-12
sources.observed_operation: Reviewed SQLite's stated atomic-commit and crash-recovery behavior.
sources.governing_conditions: One transaction appears all-or-none across a single database file; this page's detailed mechanism is for rollback-journal mode and WAL uses a different mechanism.
sources.applicability: Supports an atomic import-batch example only if inventory rows and idempotency ledger share one transactional database. Do not assume a filesystem write plus DB write is atomic.

critic_review.observed_operation: Opened SQLite atomic-commit docs: conditional transaction atomicity; detailed mechanism is rollback mode and WAL uses another mechanism.

sources.title: OWASP CSV Injection guidance
sources.version_commit: Current OWASP Community page; unversioned, accessed 2026-10-12
sources.locator: Formula interpretation risk, lines 18-28; mitigation and data trade-off, lines 51-61
sources.observed_operation: Reviewed OWASP guidance on formula interpretation when untrusted CSV is opened by spreadsheet software.
sources.governing_conditions: Spreadsheet applications may interpret formula-leading cells; suggested prefix mitigations change stored cell content and can vary by application; there is no universal safe CSV sanitization strategy.
sources.applicability: The importer should parse and render values as inert text and must not pass supplier data through a formula engine. If a future export is added, it needs a separate explicit safe-export policy and tests.

critic_review.observed_operation: Opened OWASP CSV Injection: formula-leading cells may be evaluated; mitigations vary and can change data; no universal sanitizer.
